name: Beatle haircut

card.summary: The Beatle haircut, or mop-top, is a 1960s mid-length, forward-combed cut with a full fringe that frames the face and softens the forehead.

quick.overview:
The Beatle haircut is the mid-length, brushed-forward style worn by the Beatles in the early 1960s, nicknamed the mop-top by British tabloids. It sits over the forehead and ears and was unusually long for its time.

People wear it to soften the forehead, add volume and frame the face, and it keeps returning in retro and indie fashion. It suits hair with enough density and a fairly straight fall.
quick.how: Hair is grown out to ear and collar level, cut in a rounded shape and combed forward into a fringe. Barbers describe it as a variation on a bowl-like layered cut. Maintenance is regular trims to hold the shape.
quick.risks: There are no health risks. The style depends on hair density, so thinning hair or a receding hairline may limit it, and wearers often style it with products to keep the fringe in place.

lead: The Beatle haircut is the style worn by the Beatles in the early 1960s: a mid-length cut combed forward over the forehead and ears. It was unusually long for its time, drew mockery from adults, and led British tabloids to call the band 'moptops'.[1]

The cut became an emblem of youth rebellion. In the United States it helped shift fashion away from the crewcut and combed-back looks toward longer hair, and many bands that formed after the Beatles' 1964 Ed Sullivan Show appearance grew their hair.[1] Writers have argued that it signalled androgyny and a less threatening masculinity to teenage fans.[1] In the Soviet Union, under Brezhnev, copying the style was considered highly rebellious, and young people were sometimes forced to have their hair cut at police stations.[1]

For appearance, wearers use the forward fringe and volume to frame the face and soften the forehead. The look was paired in the 1960s with Pierre Cardin suits and Beatle boots.[1] On the T Nation forum, a member recalls once wearing a 'full-on Beatles mop' before shaving his head.[2]

chain: Hair grown to mid-length and combed forward
Fringe and volume cover the forehead and frame the face
angle.text: The forward fringe and rounded volume frame the face and soften the forehead. Wearers also use it for its retro 1960s identity.

paras: The cut is mid-length, with hair brushed forward into a fringe and covering the ears. At its introduction it was considered long for men.[1]

The haircut became a youth symbol and was imitated widely. Researchers cited in coverage argue it signalled androgyny, and imitation in the Soviet bloc was treated as rebellion.[1] Its popularity contributed to a shift in Western men's grooming away from short back-and-sides cuts.[1]

timeline.event: The Beatles appear on The Ed Sullivan Show; many American bands that formed afterwards let their hair grow.[1]
